data.content_ref: inline:SRC_003's 'justification delta' is vulnerable to its own countercondition (boilerplate justifications) in a way that defeats the single-evaluation goal: if the panel is trained to append plausible observations to each tick, then 'Item 4 is present because [Observation X]' will correlate with objective outcomes even when the reasoning is glib, because the checklist was designed around outcome-relevant items. The target says 'a high correlation between the justification and the objective outcome, independent of the checklist's phrasing' indicates genuine gain, but in a single evaluation with one panel and one outcome there is no variance to estimate such correlation or to separate trained boilerplate from genuine evidence. The proposed delta is therefore not identifiable from the single evaluation as required; it reduces to the same outcome-tracking it is supposed to diagnose.
